utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me your Honour. I do believe with the pacing of the questions going back and forth it is becoming a little difficult for the translator to get the entire conversation in. There was just a comment by Mr. Djidic that did not end up on the transcript and I do not believe was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, Mr. Nobilo. You are thinking faster than you are able to speak. Perhaps you do not have to think about the judge and the Prosecution, but have some pity on the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Okay, I will try to speak more slowly. I asked: units of HOS in neighbouring municipalities, I mean neighbouring to Vitez, were they independent within the HVO, or were they within the composition of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe they were independent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know maybe about the situation in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew a little about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: HOS in Zenica, what was their status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HOS in Zenica, as far as I know, had a great number of Muslims in it. I believe they were even more numerous -- they out numbered the Croats, but I am not sure. After a certain period of time I believe in 1992 the HOS was moved and became part of the army. I do not know whether all members of the HOS became members of the army, or only the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your statement you said that somebody attacked the police station in Vitez. Could you tell us about it in greater detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said that the police station in Vitez was attacked. In the month of June. I also said that it was the members of the HOS who were responsible for the attack, with the co-operation of the civilian police of the HVO. After capturing the building of the police station members of the HOS left the station after -- because that happened after the Muslim policemen had already been expelled and only Croats were employed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that HOS cooperated with the civilian police, what kind of co-operation was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was reflected in the fact that not all policemen had been expelled from the station. That means that there had to be some sort of understanding to expel only the Muslims. The civilian police of the HVO was left intact and they continued operating throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For how long did the HOS stay in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you present to say that they remained there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the Croat policemen come to work the next day. I saw them both in town and at the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, when was the new municipality of Vitez set up, that is the Muslim municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That municipality was never established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And how about the Muslim police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was set up a month after the Muslim policemen were expelled. I am not sure, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you claim that a Muslim municipality of Vitez had never been established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where was the police station exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In which building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the building of the fire fighting society, in an abandoned room which used to house a supermarket.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know Eniz Varup?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were together in the high school. At one point he was a part-time student at the university. At another stage he was an officer in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean in the staff of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That means you were his superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not the commander of the TO then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like the usher to help me with the next document. (Handed). Mr. President, this is a copy of a writing pad. I would concentrate here only on the bits highlighted in yellow. I would like to ask you, Mr. Djidic, to place the first page first on the ELMO. So, on the first page it says Varup Eniz and reminder or memo. I am reading only the text highlighted in yellow; date 17th, month illegible, year 1992. Title "establishment of the unit of the TO Ahimici", underneath "Patriotic League". On the right page it says in capital letters "referendum". Conducted by the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina for all three nations and how important it is for us I would not even elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, President. The objection is a simple one. I believe we are in the realm of cross-examining this witness with the notes or a notebook belonging to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I agree that we can ask the source of this document from the Defence. But I am not wrong that is not really what you are asking, is it? Are you asking a question relating to the source of the document as you did with the previous document, that is the identification, as far as that goes we are going to follow the same principle as we did before. If the Defence does not supply the identification of the source the document will not be accepted for the time being as an exhibit into the case file. As for the rest, I do not see objection -- the Defence -- what exactly is your objection? That is to say, I do not understand what you are objecting to. Maybe I did not hear you right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am asking for the source, your Honour. If the source is the statement by another witness, what is going on, or attempted to be done is cross-examination of this witness from another, I suspect, another witness' notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I do not really see what can be challenged in the fact of the Defence organising the strategies as it likes. The rules of the game are the source must be identified. This is what we demanded. We cannot accept this objection. Mr. Nobilo, I give you back the floor you may continue to use the document. The Tribunal, let me remind you is the one that will decide which documents shall be used for giving reasons for its decisions. For the time being what is very important for the Tribunal is that the sources be identified. That is why we are demanding that both the Defence and the Prosecution respect the rules of the adversarial system. You may continue the cross-examination. You must say the sources. If you do not it will not be accepted by the Trial Chamber as an exhibit. All right? Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we should like to use this document in cross-examination, and we reserve the right to authenticate the document later in the proceedings and to confirm its authenticity and to reveal the source. Let us say for the moment that this is our tactics. Mr. Djidic, please turn the page. We are on page 3. That is highlighted in yellow capital letters "meeting of the TO staff Vitez". Further down it says: "Circumstances have led to such situation that is HOS and Zenga. HOS does not wish to place themselves under the control. I am sorry, do not wish to place themselves," then come two illegible words. Then follow the words "legal authority". "Today, all officers are required to state in writing whether they support this TO Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina with Bosnian Serbs. We, in Vitez, have one Ustasha group which won in Vitez. On the next page: we should -- we are required to state whether we are with them or not. Nor nip, obviously this is a quotation, sleep on that for three or four days and then we will see what we will do. We have to succumb, we have to accept and be ready to work according to the decision of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 11th April 1992, highlighted text. Lists of units. Bila, Grbavica, Sadovace, Divjak, that is in one line. Then Kruscica, Vecenska, Tolovici. Then village Ahmici, then Gacice. Next page, Mr. Djidic, thank you. Right-hand page yellow highlighted text: "Preocia company 85; Gubic platoon plus 26; Bukva platoon 26; Bila company 28, 25; Poculica company 85; Vanovinc company 85; Ahmici company 85. Following the same line, the words Pirici and Nadioci, Tolovici 26. Kruscica detachment? 200. Dubravica platoon?" It is difficult to read this word but it seems to be loop, "Lupno platoon 25; Savovace platoon 25; Murajovici platoon 25; Donja Veceriska or lower Veceriska platoon 25; "D" points the usual way to denote old Vitez or Stari Vitez detachment 230. Jranska company 85. Gacice platoon 25. D. Dubravica," most probably meaning lower Dubravica company 69. D. Selo," probably meaning Sivrino Selo. No figure in the same line and below that approximately 1,300. Next page, Mr. Djidic. On the left-hand page highlighted in yellow to facilitate the system of command establish detachments following the Territorial principle. Next line detachments first "Bila", then in smaller characters "Sabovace, Buka, Djviak, Murajovici. Roman figure 2 in capital letters Vitez Stari V." I assume Stari Vitez - Kolonija Rijeka. The next line says Roman figure 3 capital letters Kruscica - in smaller characters Vranska. Roman figure 4 Poculica. Then in smaller shrift in the same line it is written Vahoyihe, Lupac, Preocica. Below that Roman figure 5 Ahmici in capital letters, Dubravica in capital letters and in smaller shrift S. Selo I suppose Sivrino Selo." Below; "make an inspection and list equipment arms, rifles, pistols and lists, that is all." So, Mr. Djidic, you said that you know Eniz Varup from school and that he was also in the Territorial Defence. Were you present, if you recall it at all, at the meeting which discussed the political situation and the need for all officers to state their position honestly, whether they are in favour of the Territorial Defence, with Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sorry, not the Bosnian Serbs, the Bosnian coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the lists indicating certain villages on the territory of the municipality of Vitez do you know what these are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe those are plans indicating how many people could be mobilised, and, at that time the Patriotic League was in operation, which later came under the subordination of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If I have understood you well in each village as many people as are indicated next to the name of the village should be mobilised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume so, though this document and this memo, I do not recognise this memo, or the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you see the memo of Eniz Varupa from the first half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see a memo like this, or maybe I did not look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The question was: did you look at it? Do you recognise the handwriting, the handwriting of Mr. Varupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Mr. Djidic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question is the handwriting of Mr. Varupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not go to school with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I believe that the witness gave you an answer. Please proceed. You already received the answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have just finished with questions relating to this document. Of course we would like to tender it as evidence or at least if we can have the identification number and then we will authenticate it when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It will be filed provisionally with a provisional number but cannot be taken as an exhibit, I repeat it, until such time as you have indicated its source.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I please have the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment. For the time being I prefer that this one not be given numbers. They are not part of the case files, not registered. Do we have any kind of procedure we can use? If we have a number on it now, if the Tribunal does not accept it as an exhibit all of the numbering will be thrown off afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, we really do not. That will not necessarily happen. We number them because they are part of a procedure in the hearing. Therefore, just as a way of knowing what number is involved we will put a number down but it will not be part of a case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, we will proceed that way for this one and the previous one which would have been D16. So it is D16.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. One further question related to this document. You were in the TO, did the officers of the TO have to express in writing their loyalty to the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the Bosnian coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a process of registration on the part of all people who wished to join the TO. That document of inclusion in the TO was signed by me, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But before signing that document had you already been working in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there people working in the TO and who subsequently signed such a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was the former TO staff. The vast majority of the people working in the TO did sign that document, people of Croat nationality. I know personally that the document was signed by Jajlo Bravic and he was, for several months, in the staff when I joined the staff, and there was some other officers of Croat ethnic origin. I do not want to go into the listing of their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So such a statement had to be signed not only by officers but also by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was not a statement. It was simply accession to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But they were already members of the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding those who were already working there, they too signed, because they had been working in the former staff of the former JNA, which was, by now, the aggressor against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell me -- you said that the vast majority signed, including Croats. Were there people who did not wish to sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you recall a name as an example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority of Croats did not wish to join the TO, but there were quite a number of officers and soldiers who did. I do not recall the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But do you recall specifically a member of the staff who was a Croat who did not wish to sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure at this point in time, but I think all the Croats who were working in the staff at the time did sign, but others, other Croats who were not working in the staff did not sign. I am not quite certain about this. I am certain regarding those who continued to work in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said those who continued to work. Therefore, those who did not sign, could they continue working in the staff or in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know whether there were any such people, people who had worked in the former staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As for people outside the staff, could anybody refuse to sign this document, whatever you like to call it, and still be in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All those who signed were members of the TO. Actually the TO had still not been formed. This document was the predecessor to the formation of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But a moment ago you said that every one did not sign. First you said that all the people in the staff did not sign, then you said that all the people in the staff did sign but those outside did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I was not certain; but what I am certain of is that the majority of Croats who used to work in the former staff, TO staff, did sign that document, and they continued working for several months. They even were still working when I joined the staff. They were under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say the majority, I must conclude from this that some people did not sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I was not certain about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us examine a similar topic, but from the other side. The statement on loyalty to the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosnia. Have you seen that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you allow that that document could be compared to the same document that was required for accession to the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You have not seen the document, and you do not know the wording?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not seen it, nor do I know the wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But you look upon it negatively?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was never offered to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell me something else? What about the court and the Prosecutor's office, we have talked about the police and the army, I am asking about the judiciary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did exist in Vitez. I do not know exactly for how long it functioned, but there, too, people had to sign a document on their loyalty to Herceg-Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said you did not know for how long it functioned. Does it mean that the court stopped working for a time, the court and the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not pay attention to those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, what about the health care service, how was it functioning in the Vitez municipality? What existed in terms of medical institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a medical centre in Vitez, an infirmary in the factory, and another infirmary in Bila also in a factory there. I do not know whether there were other such infirmaries in the region. I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These three health care institutions within the Vitez municipality, were they operating autonomously within the municipality or were they part of a whole structure at the level of the state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, the MUP of Vitez, was it operationally part of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina based in Sarajevo? Did it cooperate with it? Was it part of the unified system, or were links broken off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I was not working in the MUP, but I think that the MUP in Vitez was operationally linked to the MUP in Zenica, and the headquarters was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You were a member of the highest bodies. Do you know from the reports whether there were operational links with Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know enough about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Taxation. Were taxes collected, such as the Federal, Republican State taxes, whatever you like and sent to the State Treasury?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know much about finances. Taxes were levied. What happened to those sums I do not know. Later on, taxes were collected by the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosnia and likewise I do not know where the money went.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the time prior to the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosnia you do not know whether the money was taken to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Pensions, or retirement allowances, did they come in from Sarajevo regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do not recall whether they came regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The educational system. Were schools working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1991 the schools were working, like most of the companies; and in the spring of 1992 they were also operating, but with certain interruptions, because we had overflights by aircraft when Vitez was shelled. I think that the schools stopped working in the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who paid for the expenses of the functioning of schools, the municipality or someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the social accounting or auditing service for payment settlements, the official auditing service for the settlement of payments between various companies, was it operating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was but I do not know for how long, how long the social accounting SDK was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it linked up to other parts of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with their system of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You just mentioned the shelling. You were in the TO. Did you have any shelters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had very few shelters, or rather Vitez, as a city, had a basement in virtually every building, which, when the airforce started the bombing, were used as shelters, both by Muslims and Croats, and Serbs and all other ethnic groups living in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In addition to those private shelters were there any public shelters in public buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You have described, at some length, the political talks and negotiations conducted in Vitez. In those political talks and negotiations and relationships, did Tihomir Blaskic participate in them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic very, very rarely appeared at local meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the Kotorvaros battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Kotorvaros battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I have heard about it, but I know no details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me remind you. Do you know that it was a Croat Muslim, or a Muslim Croat unit within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I heard something to that effect, but I do not know anything more. At least I cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there purely Croatian units within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I am talking from the company to the battalion level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher for his assistance, please, to show another document? (Handed).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, is this identified, identified, or is it like the two previous ones that it is not identified for the time being?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, like the -- as in the case of the previous document, I would like them to be numbered and we will confirm them later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, would you number them?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Djidic, will you please put on the ELMO this document, and I will read it: in inverted commas "The First Vitez brigade", formation of the command unit proposal. To the right the words: "HVO staff", has been written by hand. I now come to the text: "On the basis of the conclusions of the crisis staff of the municipal assembly of Vitez to form a joint unit in brackets brigade composed of members of the HVO and the TO representatives of the TO and the HVO have, as a result of their work so far, agreed on the following: first, in the initial period the HVO and the TO shall form one battalion each, which will join the Vitez brigade and become a part of it. 2. The method of formation of mixed units within the framework of a brigade shall be examined later. 3. The battalion formations have been established and their formation will be carried out subsequently. 4. The following proposal for formations and command members has been elaborated: number 1: brigade commander Franjo Nakic. Second: Deputy Commander and same time Chief of Staff Sefkjia Djidic. 3: Assistant Commander for operative affairs Mario Rajic. 4. Assistant Commander for organisation and mobilisation affairs Sifet Sivro or Muhamed Petkovic. 5. Officer in charge of General Affairs, Zenada Causevic. 6. Assistant commanders for moral and ethical work Pejo Dujmovic and Midhet Hodzic. Assistant commander for logistics Abdulati Barucija or Nusret Zukic. 8. Officer in charge of the technical service Zdeko Markovic. Officer in charge of the quarter master service Anton Nuk. 10. Officer in charge of medical service Zoran Pocrnja. 11. Officer in charge of the vetinary service Zdenko Zuljevic. 12. Officer in charge of ABHO Srecko Pavlovic. Officer of the engineering units Suljo Haseljic. 4. Officer in charge of signals Ismet Kalco. 15. Officer in charge of the artillery Blazenko Ramljak. 16. Assistant commander for intelligence affairs Ramiz Dugalic. 17. Assistant commander for security Sucic Ivo. 18. Four couriers or messengers will be appointed later. Please submit your comments and suggestion regarding this proposal. Copies supplied to one to the HVO command, one to the TO command, one to the SDA party and one to the HDZ party". On the right for the command of the Vitez brigade Salavic and beneath that Ramiz Dugalic. Finally, if you have any comments please forward the same, and if you have no objections please express your approval with your signature to the left for the HVO, for the HDZ to the right, for the TO and for the SDA. Mr. Djidic, is this the agreement that you referred to and your decision, on the formation of a joint Vitez brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the agreement we reached, but without this written in by hand at the top which said HVO, somebody put that in subsequently. I can now use it as evidence that the HVO wanted, and proved with this document that it wanted to be in command of the HVO, and this is what they insisted upon. But what you have read out is all correct, and this confirms my statement regarding the wish to establish a joint unit, which was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, you confirm the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I confirm it; and I think that more or less all the names indicated here are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So if I recall well, this was a joint proposal of both Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was drafted by officers from the TO and from the HVO, and this was the starting point for the formation of a joint brigade which would have been called "The First Vitez Brigade", with the command as indicated. However, the HVO insisted, in the period that followed, that it should be a brigade under the command of the HVO, as indicated here in the right-hand corner, probably at a later stage. And that is why we insisted that it should be HMVO, as I have already explained. I do not want to tire you with it by dwelling on it, because I have already explained this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, will you please turn to page 2. It says there: "Forwarded to the HVO command". So, what is written here, in handwriting, is surely an indication of who it was forwarded to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I do not think you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. I object to Mr. Nobilo's comment about whether or not he thinks he was clear or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. President, I was just saying that it was not clear to me, because I did not get an answer. I wanted to ask the next question. When the witness said "I think I was clear" I said that I did not find it clear for me to be able to ask the next question regarding the same subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understand that you did not particularly appreciate the witness' answer, but I can tell you that the handwritten indication was very clearly referred to and commented upon by the witness. So I do not think you have to make comments but simply to pose questions. Therefore I am asking you to pose the question, and I think on that point the witness answered. Re-phrase your question if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is what I had intended to do. Mr. Djidic, was this text submitted to the HVO command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So this is D18. If you have no other questions on this document, provisionally D18 according to the terms of what we said before, if there are no other questions about this document I suggest this hearing -- another one has to take place at 4.30. The room has to be prepared for it. We will see each other tomorrow morning at 10.00 am. (4.05 pm)
